description: Ratchet allowlist for tests/architecture/governance/test_cpp_include_direction.py. Each entry is a pre-existing include-direction violation against the fine-grained layer policy in tools/architecture/cpp_include_graph.py, identified by an exact (file, line, include spelling) fingerprint. The gate fails on any violation NOT in this list (including a line-shifted or re-worded version of a listed one, which forces a conscious re-review) and fails if a listed entry is no longer reproduced (stale-allowlist rot). None of these are include-path-only mistakes; each is a structural ownership coupling that the deferred T3 physical link-unit split (ef_core -> engine/mission/facade/content targets) is expected to resolve by relocating types or inverting the dependency, not by editing an include path. See the I38 registration entry in docs/plan/archive/repository_consolidation_completed_20260729/README.md for the full census. I41 (T3 second slice) re-evaluated all six entries and converged one (the components/weapon_common.h -> models/kalman_seeker.h entry below is removed; see docs/plan/archive/unified_architecture_program_completed_20260727/t6_residual_ledger.md section 7 for the full six-item evaluation matrix and the I41 registration entry in docs/plan/archive/repository_consolidation_completed_20260729/README.md for the landing summary); the remaining five keep their I38 fingerprints unchanged and gain an I41 evaluated-and-deferred attribution recorded in each entry's reason field below. Amended 2026-07-27: the runtime_contracts entry, (f), was re-adjudicated under the T1 schema-ownership option and held (see its reason field and docs/plan/archive/unified_architecture_program_completed_20260727/t6_residual_ledger.md section 7.5); its line field moved 16 -> 34 because the held adjudication is now recorded in a comment at the include site, and the entry is additionally pinned by a dedicated held-edge test in the gate file.

entries.owner: T1 DTO-family completion (re-evaluated I41, re-adjudicated under the T1 schema-ownership option 2026-07-27: held)
entries.next_gate: The T1 DTO-family-completion migration that relocates or single-sources the full nested type graph (the two batch-prep structs, the ten embedded mission aggregates, ExecutionEpisodeState, and its core/geometry SpatialRouteWaypoint dependency) with 57-def_rw binding parity across bindings_episode.cpp; nothing smaller closes this edge.
entries.reason: WorldExecutionEpisodeStepRequest's config/env_state fields (declared via the world_execution_episode_step_request.inc X-macro list at the end of this header) are typed StepEvaluationBatchConfig/StepEvaluationBatchEnvState, both owned by core/mission/episode/execution_episode_batch_prepare.h; removing this include as apparently-unused broke the ef_py build (verified 2026-07-20), confirming the contracts leaf embeds mission-owned batch-prep DTOs by value rather than the reverse. Re-evaluated at I41 (T3 second slice) with a full consumer/binding census: both types are consumed throughout core/mission/episode (execution_episode_controller.h/.cpp's evaluate/step/step_result, detail/episode_transition_runtime.h/.cpp) and core/mission/runtime/reward_runtime.h; StepEvaluationBatchEnvState alone embeds ten further mission-owned aggregate types by value (ExecutionEpisodeState, MissionObservationInputs, StepInfoInputs, SafetyRuntimeInputs, WaypointRewardInputs, ApproachRewardInputs, ConditionalObjectiveSpec, ConditionalObjectiveInputs, ObjectiveShapingConfig, FlightShapingRuntimeInputs), each field-bound individually in interfaces/python/bindings_episode.cpp and consumed from four python/rl/runtime/world_batch/** call sites. Moving either struct's physical ownership into runtime/contracts verbatim would only invert the violation (runtime_contracts's policy-allowed target set is components-only, so contracts including any of those ten mission-owned types is exactly as forbidden as this entry), and defining an independent contracts-owned transport shape would require duplicating that whole nested-type graph rather than removing the coupling -- a T1 DTO-family-completion-scale migration (the natural next single-sourcing candidate per the I31/I33/I35 lineage), not a mechanical relocation. Re-adjudicated 2026-07-27 under the T1 schema-ownership option specifically (can tools/maintenance/dto_schema own the borrowed types so both sides generate from one source byte-equivalently, per the I33 engagement-family contracts-owned-leaf pattern): held, foreclosed on three grounds verified against source. (1) The I33 pattern (generate the shared field list into a contracts-owned .inc that mission includes back, mission -> runtime_contracts being policy-allowed) works only for leaf-closed field lists of scalars/strings/vectors; StepEvaluationBatchEnvState is not leaf-closed -- it embeds the ten mission aggregates above, and ExecutionEpisodeState in turn embeds std::vector<SpatialRouteWaypoint> from core/geometry/spatial_query_runtime.h, so a contracts-located definition needs contracts -> core_geometry edges on top of contracts -> mission ones (core_geometry is also outside runtime_contracts' {components} target set). (2) The include-direction scanner counts .inc textual includes as edges (SOURCE_SUFFIXES includes .inc in tools/architecture/cpp_include_graph.py), so even schema-generated field lists that textually include core/mission/runtime/detail/*.inc (e.g. flight_shaping_shared_fields.inc, already dual-expanded into StepEvaluationBatchConfig and FlightShapingRuntimeInputs) reintroduce the violation at the new location. (3) Relocating StepEvaluationBatchConfig alone (leaf-closed if the shared flight-shaping .inc also moved to contracts/detail) would not shrink the allowlist: env_state still types against mission, this fingerprint survives verbatim, so the partial move is pure churn with ABI exposure and zero gate progress. The binding surface re-verified 2026-07-27: 57 def_rw = 15 (StepEvaluationBatchConfig) + 42 (StepEvaluationBatchEnvState) in bindings_episode.cpp, pinned by test_cpp_include_direction.py's held-edge test so binding drift forces re-adjudication. Held pending the T1 DTO-family-completion migration named in next_gate; do not reverse the dependency.
